q: The interviewer asks "Why React?" and you say "React is the best framework." What is missing from the answer?
options: The limits you had, the other options, and the cost
A longer list of React features
A benchmark number that proves React is faster
The name of a famous company that uses React
why: "The best" is a slogan. A good answer names the limits, the real options, why this one won, what it costs, and what would flip it.

q: Your team of 3 knows only PostgreSQL. A blog post says another database is faster for your case. Which do you pick, unless the speed is a real need?
options: The other database, because faster is always better
PostgreSQL, because running and fixing a new database at night costs the team more than the speed gains
Both, at the same time
Whichever one the blog author uses
why: The limits that usually decide are the team, the lifetime and who runs it. A new tool must earn its place with a job the old one cannot do.

q: Same three tools. A payments feature picks PostgreSQL. A click event stream picks DynamoDB. Why did the winner change?
options: PostgreSQL got slower
DynamoDB got better
The needs changed, so the weights changed
The interviewer changed the scores
why: Nothing about the tools changed. Safe money data and a team that knows it count most in case A. Growing writes counts most in case B.

q: After you pick a tool, what are the two things a senior answer adds?
options: A price list and a release date
The name of the person who made the tool
What you gave up, and what would change your mind
A promise that the choice is final
why: A decision with no cost sounds shallow. Say where the runner-up is better, and what would have to change for you to pick it.

q: A team of 8 builds one web app with orders and payments. What is a good starting default?
options: Ten microservices, so they can scale later
One well organised program (a modular monolith)
One service per developer
A different database for each table
why: Eight people can keep one program in their heads, and one deploy is simple. Split later, when one part needs to scale or fail on its own.

q: The interviewer's company uses Angular and you prefer React. They ask what you think of Angular. What do you say?
options: Angular is outdated
I would never use it
Say what Angular is good for, and where you would pick React instead
Change the subject
why: Show that you can reason about limits. Their choice makes sense for their lifetime and their team. Never call it wrong.
